reasoning: Natural Palestinian frame: ma + past verb, inno 'that', heek 'like this'. tawaqqa3 is an MSA-origin verb, so I keep [q], but a glottal stop (tawa''a3t) is possible in casual speech.
MSA-origin abstract noun that Palestinians use in conversation. I keep [q] as in other formal borrowings, though some speakers glottalise it.
Taa marbuta after ك is e. MSA-origin noun in common use (for example social media and events).
ع is short for على. The i of il- drops after the vowel and the l assimilates to ز, giving 3az-zaawye. Taa marbuta after ي is e.
Literally 'daughter of a maternal uncle', so a cousin on the mother's brother's side. Long aa in khaal.
Everyday word, so ق is a glottal stop: 3a'l. Also used in idioms such as 'he has sense'.
wa7iid mainly means alone, sole or only (ibn wa7iid, only son). It can mean lonely, but that is not its only sense.
ذ is pronounced d in urban Palestinian, so udun, respelled with د. Some speakers say idin or wudun; I am not fully sure which is most typical in Ramallah.
ط is emphatic, so ya3Teek. Said to someone who is working or has just done something, roughly 'may God give you strength / well done'. Palestinian form ya3Teek, not ya3Tiik.
Active participle 'importer' is mustawrid; mustawrad would be 'imported'. The English and part of speech settle the vowelling.
Final ب is doubled: shabb, plural shabaab. Common word for a young man or lad.
Palestinian fa3il verbs become fi3il, so miriD 'he got sick' (adjective mariiD 'sick'). ض is emphatic, so D.
biddi is the Palestinian 'I want'. ق is a glottal stop in 'ahwe. saade is coffee without sugar, with taa marbuta e after د.
Taa marbuta after the pharyngeal ح is pronounced a (compare raa7a). Also used for a yard or open space and for town squares.
MSA-origin political term that Palestinians use in conversation. Doubled y, then taa marbuta e after ي.
Colloquial contraction of awlaad, with the initial vowel dropped: wlaad. It means children, sons or boys depending on context.
raas 'head' + -i. The verb waja3 'to hurt' has imperfect yiwja3, so b-iwja3-ni. Ramallah speakers may also add 3am before it, and the exact vowel of the verb prefix is less certain.
Literally 'don't cut yourself off from us'. ق is a glottal stop in ti'ta3. 3anna is 'from us', with doubled n from 3an + na.
Geminate verb, 'he slapped (someone)' (from kaff 'palm'). The final ف is doubled. Darab kaff is a common alternative phrasing.
ذ becomes d in urban speech (compare kaddaab 'liar'), so kidbe. Taa marbuta after ب is e.
English loanword pronounced tenis, with a single n.
Long oo. Taa marbuta after خ is a. Everyday word for dizziness.
English loanword spelled with ب, so brinter. Some speakers say printer with p. The native word Taabi3a (طابعة) is also common.
ج is j in Palestinian (Egyptian would be g). The ending -ayh becomes -eeh. Used for the Egyptian or British pound; 'lira' is used for other currencies.
